page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v7 is an entry-tier instance within the Intel-based Dldsv7 virtual machine series, tailored for workloads requiring a lean memory footprint combined with direct local storage. It is provisioned with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The compute setup is paired with 4.0 GB of RAM (yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio), 480 MB of shared L3 cache, and modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration. Hardware resources also integrate 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while operating without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that single-core computational execution is solid, supported by the high clock speed of the Intel architecture. The instance delivers strong single-threaded data processing, achieving 35.35 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.66 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression tests. However, overall throughput is constrained by the small core count and memory bandwidth limitations. PassMark CPU scores reach 3,829.89 and stress-ng multi-core tests place the instance in the lower tier relative to larger cloud configurations. Write bandwidth across large uncached memory blocks is measured at 12.55 GB/sec, and database operations reflect low throughput at 1,008.73 operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2lds_v7 avoids overhead by provisioning a reduced memory capacity and utilizing hyperthreaded vCPUs on a single physical core. The inclusion of bundled local NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space without requiring additional attached volume provisioning. The primary architectural tradeoff is the small memory ceiling and the hyperthreaded core division, which limits suitability for concurrent multi-threaded applications or memory-heavy databases.

Microsoft Azure D2lds_v7 is best aligned with lightweight compute tasks, compression pipelines, edge proxying, microservices, and small-footprint batch processing where local scratch space and modern Intel instruction sets are prioritized over high memory density.
description: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v7 is an entry-tier virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of memory, and 118 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The processor provides advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, such as AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance in compression workloads, reaching 35.35 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside average small-model inference speeds. Because the configuration is limited to 2 vCPUs and a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, multi-threaded throughput and memory-intensive database performance remain constrained. The D2lds_v7 is primarily suited for lightweight web services, microservices, compression tasks, and localized build or test workloads requiring fast temporary scratch storage.
